items.title: Kering hires former Nike executive Francisco Ochando as group director of pricing
items.summary: Kering named ex-Nike planning director Francisco Ochando as group director of pricing across all houses and regions, institutionalizing CEO Luca de Meo's turnaround push after he said past price hikes outpaced what the market would bear; Gucci's Q3 revenue fell 6% on a comparable basis.

items.title: Kering appoints Nike exec as group director of pricing
items.summary: UK retail trade coverage of the Ochando appointment, framing it as Kering formalizing a group-wide pricing architecture after Gucci cut prices 15-30% on select handbags, sneakers and apparel this year.

items.title: Gucci Discount Strategy Puts Pressure On Luxury Rivals. Louis Vuitton Isn't Following
items.summary: Forbes analyzes Gucci's decision to cut handbag prices by up to 30% and add 16 new sub-$2,000 bag styles as a break from the industry taboo on reversing list prices, noting Louis Vuitton is holding firm over fears of brand-value damage even as both houses depend on aspirational shoppers.

items.title: Gucci lowers prices: Luca de Meo's strategy
items.summary: Italian trade outlet details de Meo's plan to stabilize Gucci's average price band between 2,000 and 3,000 euros via a roughly 20% cut on carry-over items, paired with a billion-euro inventory reduction and faster replenishment cycles, while cautioning the turnaround is not yet complete.

items.title: Kering stock: Goldman Sachs cuts Gucci forecast for Q4
items.summary: Goldman Sachs cut Kering's price target from 230 to 215 euros and revised its Gucci Q4 organic sales forecast to a 4.3% decline versus a previously expected 1% decline, citing weak retail traffic, while keeping a neutral rating and flagging possible 2027 recovery room.

items.title: Gucci Brings Latest Retail Concept to the U.K. Via Harrods
items.summary: Gucci's relocated 1,170-square-foot womenswear boutique at Harrods, which opened November 13, debuts the Demna-era 'store show' concept in the UK for the first time, following the Paris Avenue Montaigne flagship, drawing on Italian Renaissance palazzo spatial logic developed with Francesca Bellettini.

items.title: Inside Gucci's new Harrods boutique, an ode to Italian design
items.summary: Design-focused walkthrough of the new Harrods boutique's midcentury Milanese references and discovery-oriented layout, treating it favorably as a design statement rather than a hard sales story.

items.title: Gucci relocated Harrods boutique takes new concept to UK for first time
items.summary: Trade-press rundown of the Harrods relocation as part of Gucci's broader strategy of fewer, bigger, more prestigious stores, paired with the ongoing program of net store closures (125+ targeted group-wide by year-end 2026).

items.title: Gucci cuts prices, but will Chinese shoppers return?
items.summary: Jing Daily reports Gucci's Mercato tote fell about 22% and the Ophidia mini bucket bag about 29% in China, but early Xiaohongshu reaction is lukewarm, with one user noting Gucci products cost only a few thousand yuan a few years ago, undercutting the discount's psychological impact.

items.title: Fans Are 'Disappointed' Over Mariah Carey's 'Depressing' Gucci Holiday Campaign & 'Boring' Styling
items.summary: Roundup of negative social-media reaction to Gucci's Mariah Carey holiday campaign, with viewers on TikTok and Instagram calling the Harmony Korine-directed ad cold, emotionless and dated; one comment compared the aesthetic to 'JCPenney trying to be luxury.'

items.title: TikTok user reactions to Gucci x Mariah Carey holiday ad
items.summary: Aggregated TikTok comment sentiment under the Gucci holiday campaign describes the spot as 'cold,' 'boring,' 'depressing' and lacking festive energy; one widely cited comment reads: 'I would not attend that party. I'm scared.' No independently verifiable like/view counts found.

items.title: WWD on X: Front Row at Gucci Cruise 2027 in Times Square
items.summary: WWD's X post on celebrity front-row attendance (Kim Kardashian, Mariah Carey, Lindsay Lohan) at Demna's Cruise 2027 show; included for context on ongoing ambassador/celebrity buzz pattern, though dated outside the fresh window and thus weighted accordingly.

items.title: Gucci quality concerns
items.summary: Active PurseForum thread where members swap recent experiences of hardware tarnishing, loose stitching and strap peeling on newer Gucci leather goods purchased in the current product cycle, several explicitly comparing current output unfavorably to pre-2020 construction.

items.title: Appreciation for Gucci quality
items.summary: Counter-thread on PurseForum where members push back on the quality-decline narrative, sharing positive ownership experiences with recent Gucci bags; included to balance the negative quality thread and reflect the forum's genuinely mixed community sentiment.

items.title: Gucci Bamboo feel cheated
items.summary: Mumsnet style-and-beauty thread where a poster describes feeling 'cheated' after a Gucci Bamboo fragrance purchase failed to perform as sampled in-store, with other users chiming in about inconsistent longevity across Gucci's fragrance line - a value-for-money complaint pattern distinct from the handbag price story.

items.title: Gucci Cuts Prices, Louis Vuitton Holds Firm: how shoppers are reacting online
items.summary: Secondary aggregation of online consumer discussion contrasting Gucci's price cuts with Louis Vuitton's refusal to budge, noting split reactions: some shoppers welcome more accessible entry prices, others read the cuts as confirmation the brand was previously overpriced and now looks 'discounted,' denting desirability.

items.title: Inside Gucci's Paris Palazzo, a Blueprint for Its Retail Revamp
items.summary: BoF's assessment of the Avenue Montaigne flagship as the template for Gucci's international retail revamp under Demna and Bellettini, quoting Bellettini calling the Paris debut 'a very bold move' meant to reach both locals and destination shoppers; independent trade judgment, not brand-supplied copy.

items.title: Gucci Cuts Prices, LVMH Considers Following Suit: The Luxury Industry Faces a Decline in Customer Loyalty
items.summary: French-language-adjacent trade coverage frames Gucci's price cuts as evidence of an industry-wide crisis of customer loyalty after years of markup, reporting that LVMH is internally discussing whether to follow with its own corrections.

items.title: Why discounts, store closures may not be enough for Gucci as China's luxury slowdown bites
items.summary: Argues Gucci's price cuts (Padlock bag down 30% in France, from 3,500 to 2,450 euros) and store-closure program face a structural demand problem - sluggish traffic and more discerning shoppers - that pricing alone will not fix, a skeptical read on the turnaround's near-term odds.

items.title: Gucci unveils a new side of itself on Avenue Montaigne
items.summary: Coverage of the four-floor, 1,480-sqm Paris flagship opening October 30 as the first full expression of Demna/Bellettini's new retail concept, framed as central to Gucci's attempt to reverse a prolonged sales slump via fewer, larger, more immersive stores.

collection_notes: No major-EU-national-daily (Times/Guardian/BBC/Le Monde/Le Figaro/Corriere/FAZ/Der Spiegel/El Pais) original Gucci coverage surfaced for the 2026-11-24 window via public search; EU signal this cycle is dominated by trade press (WWD, BoF, nss, FashionNetwork, Jing Daily), financial wires (ad-hoc-news, Forbes) and community/SNS threads. Critical-angle searches (price-hike backlash, quality complaints, resale drop, boycott, overrated/lost-its-way, store closures, earnings miss) returned substantive results this cycle - the pricing-reversal story (Ochando appointment, Goldman downgrade, lukewarm Chinese reaction, PurseForum quality thread, Mariah Carey campaign backlash) gives real negative/skeptical weight, avoiding a purely promotional pool. Reddit-specific EU threads did not surface via public search today (site-search returned no indexed EU-relevant Gucci threads); PurseForum and Mumsnet (both T3/community, EU registry) did surface and are included. X/Twitter and Instagram brand-official posts were visible only via secondary press aggregation, not direct platform access, so engagement metrics are null throughout per the no-fabrication rule. One item (EU-012, Cruise 2027 X post) is outside the 14-day freshness window and is flagged as context-only / heavily down-weighted by the index's recency decay, not a fresh signal.
